engine.name: TinyEMU
engine.license_summary: MIT core; slirp/ 2-clause BSD; sha256.c public domain (LibTomCrypt); aes.c public domain (Rijndael reference). No GPL/LGPL content. See LICENSE-INVENTORY.md.

patches.purpose: Convert guest-poweroff exit(0) in riscv_machine.c into an observable poweroff_requested flag (library must not terminate the host process). MIT-compatible modification.

Recoverable create failures: iomem.c guest-RAM allocation returns NULL instead of exit(1); riscv_machine.c copy_bios returns 0/-1, checks kernel/initrd bounds before memcpy (upstream copied first) and releases the partial machine. Must be applied after 0001 to the same riscv_machine.c copy.

Treat the FENCE family as the no-op ordering hint it is: accept FENCE.TSO (0x8330000f) and reserved fm encodings, and ignore the unused imm/rs1/rd fields of fence.i (Zifencei). Upstream trapped FENCE.TSO as illegal, which made Debian 13 libapt-pkg die with SIGILL (apt http/https methods).

Per-VM slirp state: move the wall-clock cache (curtime), timer flags (time_fasttimo/last_slowtimo/do_slowtimo), DNS cache (dns_addr/dns_addr_time/dns_addr_stat) and the select() scratch fd_set pointers into struct Slirp; make get_dns_addr() take its Slirp explicitly (no thread-local current-instance). No slirp state is shared between instances any more; slirp_init_once() (the only remaining process-wide state, the constant loopback_addr) now uses pthread_once (InterlockedCompareExchange on Windows). Enables two independent networked VMs on two host threads.
patches.applies_to: slirp/slirp.h, slirp/slirp.c, slirp/socket.c, slirp/udp.c, slirp/ip_icmp.c, slirp/tcp_subr.c, slirp/main.h, slirp/libslirp.h of the pinned tarball

patches.purpose: Enforce 9p export-root containment structurally instead of by path-string validation: the share pins its root on root_fd (O_RDONLY|O_DIRECTORY|O_NOFOLLOW) and every fid is either a contained directory fd or a contained directory fd plus one single component; walk/open/create/mkdir/symlink/mknod/link/rename/unlink/readlink/setattr use fstatat/openat/... *at() calls with AT_SYMLINK_NOFOLLOW/O_NOFOLLOW, so '..', '/', absolute paths, guest-created symlinks and in-share renames can never resolve outside the export. FIFOs, sockets and device nodes are returned as metadata but never opened or truncated (EOPNOTSUPP), so a blocking host FIFO cannot freeze a run_slice thread. Path strings remain for diagnostics/readdir only.
patches.applies_to: fs_disk.c of the pinned tarball, after 0003

patches.purpose: Make the guest-reachable fatal paths in virtio.c recoverable per instance: unknown virtio-blk request types complete with VIRTIO_BLK_S_UNSUPP instead of the virtio_block_req_end() abort(), the guest-controlled descriptor sizes in the block/net/console paths are range-checked before use, unchecked mallocs return an error instead of writing through NULL, allocate failures in the 9p walk/read/write/readdir handlers answer a 9p error, and replies with an empty payload (Tclunk/TRflush/Tfsync) are still sent (a missing reply would hang the guest). Remaining upstream abort()s are internal invariants (fixed result-buffer sizes, device-registered access widths) and are documented in PHASE2_adapter.md.

trimmed_out: riscv_cpu.c as RV128 (CONFIG_INT128 off; RV64+RV32 only)
fs_net.c/fs_wget.c/fs_utils.c/block_net.c (HTTP network filesystem; CONFIG_FS_NET off) -> drops libcurl+OpenSSL
aes.c/sha256.c (only referenced by the HTTP filesystem path)
KVM: not present on the RISC-V path upstream (x86-only)
engine.patches_note: The integrated app vendor tree applies the full 0001-0008 set (0003/0004 are tracked there as part of the same series). The vendor script must: apply 0001 then 0002 to the same riscv_machine.c copy, 0003 then 0007 to the same fs_disk.c copy, 0005 to riscv_cpu_template.h, then 0004/0006/0008, and rebuild VENDORED-SHA256SUMS (--check re-applies patches). 0005 changes riscv_cpu_template.h, so the tree that compiles riscv_cpu.c must include the patched header; the qualification Makefile copies riscv_cpu.c + the header into $(BUILD) so the quoted include resolves to the patched copy. 0006 also edits slirp headers, so the qualification build compiles the patched slirp copies from $(BUILD)/slirp (not the pristine tree).

license_files.note: MIT text verbatim from the pinned tarball; the slirp COPYRIGHT is restored verbatim from the QEMU v3.1.0 archive because the tarball omits it. See licenses/README.md.

smoke_demo_image.name: TinyEMU RISC-V demo disk (buildroot, qualification smoke only - NOT the target userland)
smoke_demo_image.license_note: Demo guest contains GPL-licensed software (Linux kernel, busybox). It is qualification tooling, never shipped in the app. Exact boot loader/kernel revisions, patches and kernel config are recorded in docs/FLOE_LINUX_GUEST_IMAGE_MANIFEST.md; see also LICENSE-INVENTORY.md.

target_userland.name: Debian 13 (trixie) riscv64 nocloud cloud image (daily)
target_userland.pinning: daily image - resolved + SHA512 recorded by the qualification workflow at run time (see .github/workflows/tinyemu-linux-qualification.yml); not bit-pinned here because Debian rotates daily builds
target_userland.license_note: Guest packages are a mix of licenses including GPL. They are installed inside the emulated guest and are governed by their own licenses + source-availability obligations; the host app ships none of them. See docs/FLOE_LINUX_GUEST_IMAGE_MANIFEST.md for the remaining distribution gaps (no package->source manifest yet, daily image not digest-pinned).
